review_evidence: README identifies ProofNet-IR as an experimental verified proof-geometry intermediate representation and documents exact formal guarantees for checker correctness, sequentialization, scheduler invariants, and proof reconstruction.

Inspection of ProofNetIR/DesequentializationSoundness.lean finds substantive theorems proving fragment formula consistency, structural well-formedness, switching correctness, executable checker acceptance, exact conclusion recovery, and totality consequences for checked desequentialization.

The unit contains 195 primary formal files spanning proof-net semantics, graph theory, sequentialization, unification, scheduler invariants, canonicalization, and LeanProp; this is dense unique formal prior art.
summary: Retain ProofNet-IR as a large verified proof-net and proof-reconstruction formalization with substantive semantics and correctness theorems.

rules.rationale: This is a trust-audit script. Its only commands are `#print axioms <name>` for theorems that other indexed files declare, and scripts/audit_axioms.py parses the output. In search it only repeats theorem names already present in their owner files.

summary: All 176 files are Lean 4. I surveyed the root modules, ProofNetIR/, ProofNetIR/Figure7/ and consumer-v10-candidate-smoke/, and counted declaration keywords and #eval/#guard/#print commands in every file. Only two files have zero declarations: ProofNetIR.lean (the import-only root aggregator, retained under FILTER-007 because no auxiliary navigation channel is verified) and ProofNetIRAxiomAudit.lean, a 1555-line list of `#print axioms` commands that a Python trust-audit script parses. That audit file declares, states and proves nothing, so it is excluded. The library files state and prove proof-net correctness, scheduler, unification and cost-bound theorems. The *Tests, search, benchmark, corpus and audit executables hold private theorems, examples and definitions that use the library, so they stay searchable.
